content:
Anya: heads up — noticed API reference example for GET /chat/messages shows "timestamp": 1699999999 (int) in the response example but the runtime actually returns RFC3339 strings.
Mike: thanks — yes runtime emits strings like "2026-03-22T18:42:00Z". Old example is stale after the schema change.
Anya: created a docs PR with proposed fixes: update OpenAPI response schema to `string` format: date-time, update sample payloads, and patch the Go SDK snippet that parses timestamp as int64.
DocsBot: lint: samples/openapi/chat_messages_response.json: timestamp example type mismatch -> expected string
Jordan: do we need a migration note for customers who parse timestamp as unix? Might be only a few.
Sam: short note in the API reference changelog should be enough. no breaking runtime change but SDKs may need updates.
Anya: here's the proposed sample in docs to replace current one:
```
{
  "id": "msg_01F...",
  "user": "alice",
  "text": "hi",
  "timestamp": "2026-03-22T18:42:00Z",
  "metadata": {}
}
```
Mike: and Go SDK snippet currently shows `ts, _ := strconv.ParseInt(resp.Timestamp, 10, 64)` — that will break. We should update to:
```
// new Go parsing
import "time"

 t, err := time.Parse(time.RFC3339, resp.Timestamp)
 if err != nil {
   return nil, fmt.Errorf("parse timestamp: %w", err)
 }
```
Jordan: also update docs example request/response headers to include `Content-Type: application/json` and `X-Request-Id` in sample — saves support tickets.
Anya: agreed. I'll push the header examples in the same PR.
Sam: assign PR to Mike for SDK snippet review, Jordan for changelog blurb, and DocsBot will run lints on push.
DocsBot: PR #4821 created by Anya — checks queued. https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4821 :thumbsup: 
Anya: action items: (1) update OpenAPI schema (string/date-time) (2) replace response samples (3) update Go SDK snippet + add a note in migration guide (4) add header examples (5) link PR in release notes. I'll follow up in the PR comments.
Mike: will review SDK part today.
Jordan: will write a 1-paragraph migration note.
Sam: thanks everyone :rocket:
